key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum circuits can be compiled to preserve SU(2) symmetry exactly, avoiding symmetry-breaking errors that standard Clifford+T synthesis can introduce.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable and resource-efficient quantum simulation of symmetric many-body systems, with direct relevance to Heisenberg, lattice gauge, and quantum chemistry / Fermi-Hubbard workloads.
method: Uses a symmetry-preserving fault-tolerant compilation framework for SU(2)-symmetric time evolution.
Identifies a number-theoretic obstruction to exact symmetry-preserving unitary Clifford+T approximation and bypasses it with measurement plus feed-forward.
Constrains synthesis errors to the symmetry-preserving operator algebra instead of introducing symmetry-breaking perturbations.
evidence_signal: In Heisenberg transport simulations, the symmetry-preserving compiler matched the expected transport exponent at the same T-count where standard synthesis failed, and achieved about a 5x T-count reduction when both methods were tuned to equal accuracy.
watch_item: The approach relies on measurement and feed-forward, so practical gains will depend on hardware support, adaptive control latency, and overhead from mid-circuit measurements.
